## Question 1


```{r}
students <- data.frame(
  Student = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"),
  Exam_Score = c("85", "92", "78", "NA", "88", "95"),
  Study_Hours = c("5", "8", "3", "6", "NA", "10")
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: false
s2 <- students |>
  mutate(Study_Hours = as.numeric(Study_Hours))

str(s2)
```

## Question 2

Run the code below. You can see the relationship between Flipper Length, Body Mass, and Species. There is something misleading / incorrect with this graph. In 2-3 sentences, identify the issue and explain why it is incorrect/misleading.

Note: You do not need to fix the issue or change any of the code.

Note: In this scenario, the truncated y-axis is not considered misleading.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
penguins |>
  drop_na(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g, species) |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = flipper_length_mm,
      y = body_mass_g,
      color = as.numeric(species)
    )
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_gradient(
    low = "yellow",
    high = "red",
    breaks = 1:3,
    labels = c("Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Penguin Body Mass relationship with Flipper Length, by Species",
    x = "Flipper Length (mm)",
    y = "Body Mass (g)",
    color = "Species"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Question 3 

Questions 3 and 4 use the `diamonds` dataset from the `ggplot2` package. For more information on the dataset, and the variables used. 

Run the code below. Based on the rules/discussions we have had around data visualizations in class, there are > 3 issues with the way these data are being displayed. Make a bulleted list that identified **three** issues. Next, make a new code chunk and copy the code used to create this plot into your new code chunk. In your new code chunk, fix the issues you identified to make this plot more effective. 

```{r}
#| echo: false 
#| eval: true
diamonds |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = carat,
      y = price,
      color = cut
    )
  ) +
  geom_point(
    size = 4,
    alpha = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Diamonds",
    x = "Carat",
    y = "Price (US dollars)",
    color = "Cut"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("red", "blue", "green", "purple", "orange")
  ) 
```
